new_diagnostic.comparison: Predict same target GPS altitude bins from own bird×Wstar distribution against own pooled distribution × population-common Wstar odds estimated from at least two OTHER biological birds, same study/species, 50km cell and same YYYY-MM; exclude focal bird and the entire target date, equal donor days/birds.
new_diagnostic.predeclared_remaining_fixed_attributes: 4 frozen study-species panels, Wstar day states, 50km, day median centered ten bins, 20 scored fixes/day, >=2 low and >=2 high days, >=10 birds, 999 within bird×month Wstar label exchange, >=950 valid draws, four-study Holm including unavailable p=1
new_diagnostic.inferential_scope: Post-outcome exploratory model comparison; nominal exchangeability further weakened when permutation changes eligible individual count.

scientific_reading.direct: Both original G. fulvus source panels retain primary thermal-conditioned altitude-shape predictability, but when prediction is compared against a species-shared thermal-response model, neither provides independent confirmation of a bird-specific thermal reaction. In one study the raw extra gain is almost zero and below shuffled reference; in the other +0.02813 raw but its null-excess +0.00763 has exploratory Holm p=0.268.
keep_uncertainty: Lack of supported incremental individual-specific reaction does not establish common shared thermal response as uniquely causal; a model comparison's unsupported contrast is not an equivalence test.
Same environmental sources are all post-outcome, not new animals/studies, so even exploratory nominal p below 0.05 would not prove a generalized individual×wind rule.
Strict other-animal, same-month, other-date source comparison produces 0 and 8 birds in G. africanus and G. coprotheres; these are structurally unavailable, not biologically zero.
Null shuffles alter eligible-bird support, especially study 122120597 observed24 versus null14–23, so permutation exchangeability and its p-value need caution.
Shared species response model is one multiplicative adjustment with Jeffreys smoothing; source GPS height may contain terrain and nonadditive tag errors and flight-mode mixtures.
scientific_reading.new_hypothesis: Predictive wind context may be largely shared among species members, while stable individual reaction norms require stronger evidence from independent same-cell same-state repeated birds and physical air/flight mode measurements.
scientific_reading.future_primary: Pre-freeze and test in independent ≥10-bird per-species study with GPS heights, independent Wstar/airflow, verified behavior labels, device-quality, full bird×date overlap, and an explicitly shared-species environment baseline.
